newsitem.title: USA: ADM Gulf loadings disrupted by Greenpeace.
newsitem.headline: ADM Gulf loadings disrupted by Greenpeace.

text.p: Protestors from environmental group, Greenpeace disrupted grain loadings at Archer Daniels Midland's grain terminal at Destrehan, La., on Thursday, according to Greenpeace and an ADM source.
"They (protestors) are all over the place out here," said an ADM employee at the terminal, who declined to be named.
"We are not loading right now. We have the police department out here," the employee said before hanging up.
An ADM spokesman at the company's headquarters in Decatur, Ill., was not available for comment.
The Destrehan terminal has storage capacity of more than six million bushels and a loading rate of 50,000 bushels per hour, according to industry sources.
Greenpeace said in a statement on Thursday morning that its activists had "occupied" the Destrehan facility and halted loadings to protest exports of genetically altered soybeans.
"Today's action marks Day Four of the week-long Greenpeace protest against the release of genetically engineered soybeans into the marketplace," the statement said.
The soybeans are engineered to tolerate Monsanto Co's "Roundup Ready" herbicide.

Greenpeace said its activists, wearing white hard hats and blue overalls with "Genetic Experiment" written on them, climbed into and attached themselves onto 200-foot-long barges at the terminal loaded with soybeans.
The ADM employee, however, said the facility was loading corn when the protestors arrived.
Greenpeace also said additional activists dressed in white uniforms chained themselves to the front entryway of the grain facility.
